slides.say: Use ref gives you a plain JavaScript object. Let us look inside.
Pass the initial value as the only argument. You get back an object with a single property: current.
Current is mutable. You read it and write it directly, and the change is immediate. No setter, no snapshot.

slides.text: Same object every render. Think: state without a setter.
slides.say: React returns the same object on every render. You can picture it as a state variable whose setter you never use.

slides.text: Use for: timeout IDs, DOM nodes, values not needed for JSX.
slides.say: Use refs for timeout IDs, DOM elements, and other values that are not needed to calculate the JSX.
